No, **Bidvest Medical** does not sell or distribute consumer or patient-facing wearable medical devices (like continuous glucose monitors, smart ECG patches, or consumer fitness/health trackers).

Instead, Bidvest Medical (a division within the broader [Bidvest Group](https://bidvest.co.za/)) focuses on heavy diagnostic imaging tech and mobile institutional screening infrastructure. [](https://www.globaldata.com/company-profile/the-bidvest-group-ltd/)

- **Digital Radiography:** Distributing advanced hardware like Konica Minolta digital X-ray systems and lightweight cassette detectors.

- **Mobile Health Units:** Engineering and equipping custom mobile screening trucks (such as tuberculosis and occupational health screening vehicles).

- **Institutional Technology:** Supplying high-tech medical showrooms and specialized hospital/industrial diagnostic gear rather than personal wearable monitors.

If you are looking for a specific type of **wearable medical device** or a distributor that carries patient-monitoring technology, let me know what **region or country** you are searching in so I can point you toward the right suppliers.

The monthly cost of a Continuous Glucose Monitor (CGM) averages
between
$100 and $300 with pharmacy discounts or manufacturer coupons
, but can range from
$0 to over $500
depending heavily on your insurance coverage and the specific brand you choose.
GoodRx
Cost Breakdown by Insurance Status
With Commercial Insurance / Medicare
: Most covered patients pay between
$0 and $60 per month
. Major brands like the Abbott FreeStyle Libre are covered by most commercial insurance plans for patients who take insulin or experience severe hypoglycemia.
Without Insurance (Out-of-Pocket Retail)
: If you pay standard cash retail prices at the pharmacy, supplies can cost anywhere from
$160 to $500 per month
Healthline
Without Insurance (Using Manufacturer Coupons)
: You can drop cash costs significantly by using pharmacy discount cards or coupons directly from the manufacturer
. For example, Abbott's program can drop prescription FreeStyle Libre costs to roughly
$70 to $75 per month
for a 30-day supply of sensors.

Hidden Costs to Keep in Mind
Transmitters
: Older systems (like the Dexcom G6) require a standalone transmitter every 3 months, which adds
$200 to $350
to your annual costs. Newer models like the Dexcom G7 and FreeStyle Libre 3 integrate the transmitter directly into the disposable sensor.

Receivers
: While you can use a free smartphone app to read your data, a dedicated physical reader device costs a one-time fee of
$100 to $400
if you choose to use one.
